QUOTE: "**Compile-time macros.** Define `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO` ... **Runtime registration.** Define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free)`" and "With the compile-time macros set, `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is compiled out (`platform.c:20-22`); calling it then is a link error"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer distinguishes the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair, and says the setter is compiled out when the macros are defined. That makes the two mutually exclusive.
